name: MyAML: JSON Builder
reframe: Lets non-technical teams build release notes and other JSON through a simple form, so developers aren't pulled away from their own work.

overview.purpose: Developers kept stopping their own work to hand-write release notes and other JSON documents for the rest of the team. I built MyAML so the people who need those documents can produce valid JSON themselves.
overview.audience: Business analysts, project managers and other non-technical staff who need structured JSON such as release notes, plus the developers or leads who design the reusable structures for them.

solves.title: Removes a developer bottleneck.
solves.detail: Non-technical staff create release notes and other structured JSON themselves, so developers no longer write it by hand.

solves.title: No JSON knowledge needed.
solves.detail: Users fill in a normal form and the app writes valid, properly formatted JSON. There are no missing commas, unclosed brackets or broken quotes.

solves.title: Plain-language data types.
solves.detail: Fields are labelled "Text", "Whole number", "Yes/No", "Group", "List" and "Choice", each with a short example, instead of string, integer and boolean.

solves.title: Ready-made release-notes template.
solves.detail: The app opens with version, date, tasks and sub-tasks already set up, so the most common request works straight away.

solves.title: Reusable structures.
solves.detail: A developer or lead designs the structure once in the Blueprint tab, and anyone can fill it in from the Editor tab as often as needed.

solves.title: Catches mistakes early.
solves.detail: Empty required fields are flagged in the form and highlighted in the JSON preview, blank or duplicate field names are marked, and a status bar shows whether the output is valid.

solves.title: Easy hand-off.
solves.detail: One click copies the JSON or downloads it as a dated .json file, ready to send to the development team.

learned.title: Schema-driven dynamic forms.
learned.detail: Built a form engine in Angular 20 with standalone components that builds itself from a user-defined schema, using a recursive template that handles objects inside arrays inside objects to any depth.

learned.title: Reactive state with RxJS.
learned.detail: Centralised state with BehaviorSubject and combineLatest keeps the Blueprint, the Editor and the live preview in sync.

learned.title: Data-preserving schema changes.
learned.detail: Renaming a field or changing its type keeps the values already entered instead of resetting them.

learned.title: A custom JSON tokenizer.
learned.detail: Powers the preview's line numbers, syntax colours and per-line error highlighting, with caching so it doesn't redo the work on every change.

learned.title: Recursive algorithms.
learned.detail: Used for validation, nesting-depth calculation and node counting in the status bar.

learned.title: Theming with design tokens.
learned.detail: A custom PrimeNG theme built from design tokens and SCSS variables, with a "developer terminal" look.

learned.title: Accessibility in practice.
learned.detail: Keyboard navigation between tabs, visible focus outlines, tooltips on icon-only buttons, reduced-motion support and a responsive phone layout.

learned.title: Shipping the details.
learned.detail: In-app release notes (the app uses the same kind of notes it helps produce), Angular Router routes, SEO metadata, and a move of the unit tests to Vitest.

name: Handmade Candle E-commerce
reframe: A full-stack store for a small handmade-candle business — checkout built so a failed payment can never become a paid-looking order.

caseStudy.problem: A small handmade-candle business needed its own online store to sell directly to customers.
caseStudy.constraints: Solo project, built in my own time for a friend's home business. I owned everything from database design to deployment, with no team to review my code, and the owner isn't technical, so managing products and orders had to be simple and hosting costs had to stay low.
caseStudy.role: Full-stack: ASP.NET Core API with Dapper and SQL Server, and the React storefront.
caseStudy.architecture: React storefront -> ASP.NET Core Web API -> Dapper -> SQL Server
caseStudy.technicalChallenge: Handling failed or cancelled payments correctly, so an order record is never created for a cart that didn't actually complete checkout.
caseStudy.decision: Split checkout into separately shippable pull requests — cart persistence, address capture, payment integration, order confirmation — instead of one large change, so each piece could be tested and shipped on its own while working solo. Chose Dapper over Entity Framework Core because the schema is small and checkout depends on a few critical queries. Writing that SQL by hand made it clear exactly when an order, its stock updates and its payment status are written in one transaction, and Dapper's low overhead suited cheap hosting.
caseStudy.result: The business has its own storefront to sell directly to customers instead of relying only on word of mouth and social media messages. Reviewing my own payment-integration PR before merging caught the failed-payment case before release, so a declined or cancelled payment leaves the cart intact and never creates an order.
caseStudy.learned: Working alone doesn't mean skipping process: splitting checkout into small PRs and reviewing each one as if someone else wrote it is what caught the payment bug before a real customer could hit it.

name: ERS: Event Registration System Admin Portal
reframe: Gives event organisers one portal to run large events from start to finish, from the first registration to check-in on the day, without needing developers for each event.

overview.purpose: Our organisation runs many events, from small invited gatherings to large public ones with thousands of people. Each one needs registration forms, payments, accommodation, transport, emails and check-in. I'm one of the main contributors on the team building the ERS admin portal. It replaces scattered spreadsheets and one-off tools with a single place where admins set up and run every part of an event.
overview.audience: Event organisers, volunteers and regional coordinators who set up and run events, and finance, transport and accommodation teams who each look after their own part of an event. Access to each area is controlled by role.

solves.title: One portal for the whole event.
solves.detail: Event setup, sub-events, registration, payments, accommodation, transport, communication, check-in and reporting all live in one admin app, so nobody has to switch between tools.

solves.title: Handles many kinds of events.
solves.detail: Supports RSVP Open and Invited events as well as Non-RSVP Individual, Group, Family and Spouse events, each with its own rules for who can register and how.

solves.title: Registration forms without code.
solves.detail: Admins build forms from question sections, set field rules that show or skip questions based on earlier answers, and tag questions so each participant only sees the ones that apply to them.

solves.title: Fast participant onboarding.
solves.detail: CSV and Excel bulk upload checks each row against several identifiers (Email, phone, or first and last name) and tells the admin exactly which rows need fixing.

solves.title: Payments and refunds handled in-app.
solves.detail: Each event gets its own payment configuration, early-bird and participant-level discounts, accounting codes and a refund report. Currency and payment mode lock once anyone has paid, so transaction records stay consistent.

solves.title: Logistics in one place.
solves.detail: Accommodation inventory and assignment, transport assignment, driver and vehicle allocation, and airline and airport details are managed next to the registration data, not in separate spreadsheets.

solves.title: Targeted communication.
solves.detail: Reusable email templates and scheduled queues can be filtered by region, centre, zone, mandal, category or tag. Delivery errors show up in the app, so admins can fix them without asking a developer.

solves.title: Smooth event-day check-in.
solves.detail: QR-code scanning with the device camera, printable ID cards built from templates, and participant checklists make check-in quick on the day.

solves.title: Reports on demand.
solves.detail: Master, statistical, family, transport and payment reports can be filtered and exported to Excel, so coordinators get their own numbers without filing a data request.

solves.title: Safe, role-based access.
solves.detail: System roles, event roles and role mapping control who can view or edit each module and each region's data, so volunteers only see what they need.

learned.title: Working in a large, long-running codebase.
learned.detail: Contributed more than 1,700 commits since 2023 to a 50+ module Angular app with a team of around ten developers, across more than 50 versioned releases.

learned.title: Dynamic, rule-driven forms.
learned.detail: Built and extended a form engine that renders sections, table questions and conditional field rules from server-defined configuration, with reactive forms and custom validation.

learned.title: HTTP architecture with interceptors.
learned.detail: Worked with a core layer of token, API-prefix, caching and error-handling interceptors, plus authentication and permission guards and a custom route-reuse strategy.

learned.title: Reusable shared components.
learned.detail: Pulled duplicated features, such as public and private file uploads, into shared components with clear inputs and outputs, so new screens use one tested implementation.

learned.title: Working with files in the browser.
learned.detail: Parsed and validated CSV and Excel uploads, generated formatted Excel exports with ExcelJS, and rendered printable ID cards with QR codes using html2canvas.

learned.title: Rich content editing.
learned.detail: Integrated CKEditor 5 and Quill with mentions, so admins can write communication templates with placeholders that get filled per participant.

learned.title: Designing for real operational constraints.
learned.detail: Handled payment edge cases, regional date formats (DD/MM/YYYY for ANZ), cross-browser upload issues and permission rules for each region.

learned.title: Shipping and quality discipline.
learned.detail: Builds for each environment (dev, QA, UAT, prod) run through Jenkins CI, ESLint is enforced with each issue fixed by hand, and release notes appear inside the app and are written in the same JSON format that MyAML produces.
